testEnvironment:
Test environment: the snapshot is a git repository whose single commit holds
the reviewed tree — its tree hash was compared against the commit under review
when the snapshot was cut. A suite run here collects and runs what a checkout at
that commit does, so a failing or skipped test is a fact about the tree, not
about this copy of it. Its history is that one synthetic commit: 'git log',
'git diff' and every ancestry question answer about the snapshot and never about
the PR.
The Recipe's Test entrypoint and Check step do not run these merge-gating CI steps, and nothing in this review ran them: rebase-check job (pull_request-only branch-currency assertion, not meaningful in a worktree of origin/main); proc-macos job (node --test tests/proc.test.mjs on macOS) (subsumed by the full suite on this macOS host); smoke-omp job (needs pinned omp installed via bun, absent here); install-and-smoke job (needs pinned omp installed via bun and network, absent here).

survived.claim: The `--pr` pass now evicts the trees in every kept `pr<N>/run-*` root, however young, so a second review of the same PR starting while another is still running strips that live review's snapshot and copies of their installed dependencies mid-measurement.
survived.evidence: Probe in my copy: makeTree(<scratch>/pr7/run-LIVEaaaa/snapshot-abc), created seconds earlier, then `node plugin/scripts/reclaim-scratch.mjs --pr 7 --root <scratch> --apply`. Output: exit 0, receipt {"removed":[],"evicted":[{"path":".../pr7/run-LIVEaaaa/snapshot-abc","reason":"a tree in a kept review run root","ignored":["node_modules/"]}],"kept":[{..."reason":"run root modified within 7 days"}],"failed":[]}. After it, `live sibling node_modules present after: false`. The only justification in the docs and comments is that "a live review's own run root is seconds old and holds no tree yet", which covers the caller's own root and not a sibling. Same-PR runs do overlap: run-team retries under review-pr-<pr#>-b, a standalone /review-and-fix can run beside a fleet review, and the ticket itself counts three run roots at one head.
survived.suggested_fix: Evict only kept run roots that are demonstrably finished, for example ones holding review.json, or ones whose newest mtime is older than a short grace period. Or leave kept run roots to their own review's end-of-run eviction and evict only roots that review never reached.

votes.reason: Read reclaim-scratch.mjs:628-636 in the snapshot: in --pr mode every entry in `kept` is passed to evictTrees(run.path,{apply}) with no age or ownership check. Kept entries include young runs, since the reason is 'run root modified within 7 days'. evict-tree.mjs evictTrees has no age check either. It removes the ignored paths (node_modules) of every tree under the run root. So a concurrent sibling run's snapshot is stripped. I did not run the probe myself, so this rests on reading the code and the reporter's output. CWD-AUDIT: clean /Users/chris/dev/fleet-plugin (not run; I made no writes there)

Reproduced in my own copy of the snapshot. I built a young sibling run root with a tree whose node_modules/ is ignored, then ran `node plugin/scripts/reclaim-scratch.mjs --pr 7 --root <scr> --apply`. It exited 0 and evicted the tree (reason "a tree in a kept review run root", ignored ["node_modules/"]) while the run root was kept as "modified within 7 days". Afterwards the tree held only the .git entry and tracked files, and node_modules was gone. The eviction loop at reclaim-scratch.mjs:~628 covers every kept run root with no age or ownership check. The header comment's "seconds old, holds no tree yet" justification covers only the caller's own root. Nothing else guards sibling runs. The eviction is new in this PR (the evictTrees calls appear only as additions in pr.diff). I did not check whether a same-PR review really overlaps in practice. No test was run, so there is no red/green evidence line. CWD-AUDIT: dirty /Users/chris/dev/fleet-plugin — ` M docs/metrics/ticket-features.tsv`, ` M docs/metrics/tier-outcomes.tsv`. I did not touch these files and did not write inside this directory; they were already modified there.

survived.claim: evictableRunRoot compares the reported run root against `posix.join(scratch, "pr<N>")`, while the snapshot step builds the run root from the raw `${scratch}/pr${pr}/run-`. A scratch with a trailing slash or a `./` segment, which every scratch check accepts, therefore makes the end-of-review eviction skip with nothing logged while the review itself succeeds.
survived.evidence: Probe through runReview with the scripted host (as in review-core-run-end-eviction.test.mjs), scratch passed as `<abs>/scratch/` and the reported runRoot `<abs>/scratch//pr7/run-abcd1234`, the shape mktemp prints. Result: `result.head abc123`, so the review succeeded, then `node_modules still present: true logs: []`. I confirmed the shape with `mktemp -d "$D/mk//pr7/run-XXXXXXXX"`, which printed `.../mk//pr7/run-D1523rLB`, and `.../mk/./pr7/...`, which kept `./`. runnerScratchRefusal and scratchRootRefusal (fleet-dir.mjs:198-219) reject neither form.
survived.suggested_fix: Use one prefix for both: compare runRoot against the same `runRootPrefix` string snapshotMissing uses, or posix.normalize both sides. Log when a run root was reported but judged not evictable, so the skip is no longer silent.

votes.reason: Confirmed by reading and a node run. evictableRunRoot uses posix.join(scratch,`pr${pr}`), which normalizes: join('/a/s/','pr7') and join('/a/./s','pr7') both give '/a/s/pr7'. The run root is built raw as `${scratch}/pr${pr}/run-` (review-core.mjs:1094-1095), so mktemp prints '/a/s//pr7/run-X'. startsWith('/a/s/pr7/') is then false and eviction returns silently with no log. runnerScratchRefusal (review-core.mjs:950-957) rejects only '..' segments and a pr<N> ending, so a trailing slash and './' pass. I did not run the full runReview probe or any test suite. CWD-AUDIT: not run; I only read files and ran node -e, and wrote nothing in /Users/chris/dev/fleet-plugin.

Not handled elsewhere: reviewRun uses A.scratch raw (`${scratch}/pr${pr}/run-`, review-core.mjs:1093-1095) with no normalization, and evictableRunRoot (1031) compares against posix.join(scratch,'pr7'). Ran node: scratch '/a/scratch/' gives partition '/a/scratch/pr7' and runRoot '/a/scratch//pr7/run-abcd1234', startsWith(partition+'/') = false, so evictRunRoot returns silently with no log. fleet-dir.mjs scratchRootRefusal does not reject trailing slash. I did not run the full runReview probe; the claim's impact (silent skipped cleanup, review still succeeds) follows from the code. survived.claim: isTree() turns every git failure (unreadable .git, broken .git, timeout, ENOBUFS, dubious ownership) into 'not a tree', and evictTrees() neither evicts nor reports it, so the tree keeps its installed deps with failed[] empty and no SNAPSHOT_PRUNE_FAILED or review-end log.
survived.evidence: probe1.mjs against copy/plugin/scripts/evict-tree.mjs with apply:true. A: tree with `chmod 000 .git` returned {"evicted":[],"failed":[]} and node_modules still existed. B: tree with .git/HEAD renamed returned the same, node_modules still existed. In both, the tree's own ls-files path (which does report) never ran, because rev-parse failure returns false. The docs (scratch-reclaim.md) say a tree that failed is 'tried again by the next review's pass'. These trees are not marked failed, so the only signal is the disk staying full.
survived.suggested_fix: In isTree, report a rev-parse that errors or exits non-zero when `.git` exists. Treat only a successful answer naming a different toplevel as 'enclosing repository', and push {path, error} to failed for the other cases. Or have evictTrees return a third `skipped` list that reclaim-scratch prints.

votes.reason: Ran evictTrees(apply:true) from my copy of the snapshot on a tree whose .git/HEAD was renamed and which held an ignored node_modules. It returned {"evicted":[],"failed":[]} and node_modules was still there. In the snapshot source, isTree() (evict-tree.mjs:92-103) returns false when `git rev-parse` fails, so evictTrees skips the tree without adding it to failed. I did not run the chmod 000 case, the timeout or ENOBUFS cases, or the dubious-ownership case. I did not check whether the documented SNAPSHOT_PRUNE_FAILED log would fire elsewhere. Reproduced on the snapshot's evict-tree.mjs. I made a git repo with node_modules gitignored and `chmod 000 .git`, then ran evictTrees(apply:true). It returned {"evicted":[],"failed":[]} and node_modules still existed. The code agrees: isTree() returns false on any rev-parse error or non-zero status (lines 92-104), so the tree is skipped without entering failed[]. The reported line 184 is wrong; the file has 154 lines and the logic is at ~line 99. I found nothing elsewhere that handles or reports this case, and no test or doc comment that deliberately treats an unreadable .git as a non-tree. Not run: a positive control showing the same fixture is evicted when .git is readable. I also did not run the broken-HEAD variant. survived.claim: evictTrees() skips a directory it cannot list (EACCES/EPERM/ENOENT/ENOTDIR) with no failed entry, so a tree below a mode-000 or otherwise unreadable directory is never evicted and nothing says so.
survived.evidence: probe1.mjs case C: root/C/sub chmod 000, containing tree/ with ignored node_modules/. evictTrees(root,{apply:true}) returned {"evicted":[],"failed":[]} and `C tree nm exists true`. A review run root is built by agents, so a specialist copy under a directory that dropped its read bit stays installed without an error. The comment says this mirrors freshUnder(). But freshUnder's caller keeps the whole key as unknown, while this path discards it.
survived.suggested_fix: Put EACCES/EPERM into failed (as `cannot list it`) rather than skipping it, or at least count them in a `skipped` field of the receipt. Keep ENOENT/ENOTDIR as benign races.

votes.reason: Reproduced. I built root/C/sub (chmod 000) containing a git tree with an ignored node_modules/. evictTrees(root,{apply:true}) returned {"evicted":[],"failed":[]}, and node_modules still existed afterward. The catch at evict-tree.mjs:139-144 explicitly skips EACCES/EPERM/ENOENT/ENOTDIR without recording a failure. The function's own docstring says `failed` includes 'a directory that cannot be read', which contradicts the code. I ran only this direct probe, not ./agent-test. CWD-AUDIT: dirty /Users/chris/dev/fleet-plugin — ' M docs/metrics/ticket-features.tsv', ' M docs/metrics/tier-outcomes.tsv'. I did not touch these files; they were modified by other agents.

Code check only, nothing executed. evict-tree.mjs lines 138-144 read as follows. `readdirSync` is wrapped in a catch. For ENOENT, ENOTDIR, EACCES and EPERM the catch does `continue` without pushing to `failed`. Only other error codes are recorded. So an unreadable directory is skipped silently and any tree below it is never evicted, as claimed. The finding's probe run (case C) was not re-run. Lens 2: I found no other handling. A grep of tests/evict-tree.test.mjs for `000` and `EACCES` found nothing. The skip is deliberate, per the code comment, but it does not surface the skipped directory to callers. The finding's contrast with freshUnder is not checked. CWD-AUDIT: not run; I made no writes and ran only reads in /Users/chris/dev/fleet-plugin.

survived.claim: Each `--pr <N>` pass now evicts the installed deps of every kept (young) run root under pr<N>, including another review's still-running run root, and the receipt only labels it 'a tree in a kept review run root'. The code comment's assumption that a live run root 'holds no tree yet' is true only for the caller's own root.
survived.evidence: Built rs/pr7/run-LIVE0001/snapshot-x via tests/support/run-tree.mjs (node_modules present), ran `node plugin/scripts/reclaim-scratch.mjs --root rs --pr 7 --apply`. Receipt: evicted:[{path:.../run-LIVE0001/snapshot-x,reason:'a tree in a kept review run root',ignored:['node_modules/']}], kept reason 'run root modified within 7 days', failed:[]; node_modules was gone afterwards. A second review of the same PR starting while the first runs strips the first one's installed dependencies mid-run. The first review then sees test or build failures that look like its own and are reported as a PR defect.
survived.suggested_fix: Evict only run roots idle past a short grace period, or exclude the caller's own run-root family and any run root with a recent write. Or have `--pr` take a lease/idle threshold shorter than 7 days but longer than a review's life.

unverified.claim: An eviction by the `--pr` pass bumps the evicted tree's directory mtime, so a run root idle for about 6 days (for example one whose review died before its finally block ran) becomes fresh again and gets another full 7 days before the age rule removes it.
unverified.evidence: Probe tests/zz-probe2.mjs in my copy: makeTree under pr7/run-oldaaaaa, every mtime set 6 days back, then freshUnder(run, now-1d) returned null (idle). After `reclaim-scratch.mjs --pr 7 --root <scratch> --apply` evicted it, freshUnder(run, now-1d) returned `.../run-oldaaaaa/snapshot-abc` (fresh).
unverified.suggested_fix: Restore the parent directories' mtimes after removal, or document that an eviction restarts the retention clock (the evicted root is small, so the cost is low).

unverified.claim: [INFERENCE, not executed] run.runRoot takes snap.runRoot before snapshotMissing validates it, and evictableRunRoot checks only its shape. A misreported runRoot naming another existing run-* root of the same PR would therefore have that root's trees evicted in the finally block, even though the review then refuses the report.
unverified.evidence: Code read only: line 1308 assigns run.runRoot from the raw report, and snapshotMissing runs afterwards at line 1316. evictableRunRoot (1031-1041) checks the partition prefix, the run-[A-Za-z0-9]{8} shape and lstat isDirectory, and nothing ties the root to the one this run's mktemp created. No probe run.
unverified.suggested_fix: Record the run root only once snapshotMissing(snap, runRootPrefix) returns null and SNAPSHOT_RUN_ROOT matches the report, or have the eviction require the snapshot path that this run verified.

unverified.claim: The documented guarantee that a failed eviction 'never changes what the review returns or throws' is false when host.log itself throws: the log call inside evictRunRoot's catch (and the loop above it) throws out of the `finally`, replacing the review's return value or original error.
unverified.evidence: Throwaway runReview test with host.log = m => { if (/eviction/.test(m)) throw new Error('log sink closed') }, snapshot tree chmod 0555 so removal fails. Output: `P2 THREW log sink closed`, where the review had completed with head abc123 (P3, same setup with a normal log, returned abc123 and logged `eviction at the end of the review failed in ...snapshot-abc123: could not remove node_modules/: ... Permission denied`).
unverified.suggested_fix: Wrap the log calls in evictRunRoot in their own try/catch, or make the finally `try { evictRunRoot(...) } catch {}`.

unverified.claim: evictableRunRoot() rejects a snapshot-reported runRoot of the wrong shape (wrong length, symlinked partition, or lstat error) silently: no eviction and no log, so a run root that the shape check misjudges keeps its deps with nothing recorded.
unverified.evidence: Throwaway runReview test with the snapshot agent reporting runRoot `.../pr7/run-abcd123` (7 chars) with a real tree under it. runReview returned head abc123; `nm exists true`, eviction log lines: []. The existing test 'evicts nothing when the snapshot agent reported nothing, and says nothing about it' pins the null-report case.
